title: Netskope One Enterprise Browser, Now With Agentic Capabilities
summary: For a long time, the enterprise browser had a tidy job description. Give contractors and people on personal laptops safe access to company apps, stop data
body_markdown:
For a long time, the enterprise browser had a tidy job description. Give contractors and people on personal laptops safe access to company apps, stop data walking out through copy, paste, and print, and save the cost of a virtual desktop. Netskope One Enterprise Browser has done that job for our customers, and it still does.


Then the browser picked up a second job. People now chat with AI in one tab while pasting company data into it from another. They install AI extensions that can read every page they open. And agents have arrived, clicking, typing, and sending things on a person’s behalf, using that person’s own logins. Nearly half of AI users


[still rely on personal AI apps](https://www.netskope.com/resources/cloud-and-threat-reports/cloud-and-threat-report-2026) , and


[91% of organisations can’t stop a risky agent action before it executes](https://www.netskope.com/resources/reports-guides/ai-risk-and-readiness-report) .


So we’ve upgraded Netskope One Enterprise Browser to handle both jobs. The secure access it already provides is still there. What’s new is a set of agentic browser capabilities built into the same browser.


## What was Netskope One Enterprise Browser doing already?


Netskope One Enterprise Browser is Chromium-based and hardened by Netskope. We shrink the threat surface by removing features that aren’t needed for work, let admins configure settings such as developer tools access, and add impersonation protection, anti-tampering, encrypted critical assets, and admin-approved extensions. It steers unmanaged devices to Netskope security service edge (SSE) protections, applies controls for copy/paste, print, screenshots, text input, uploads, encrypted downloads, screen sharing, and watermarks, and gives contractors self-service access to the apps they need. Customers use it for bring your own device (BYOD) programmes, contractor onboarding, and moving web workloads off virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI).


## New: An agent every employee can use, on your terms


The first addition to our Enterprise Browser is an agentic assistant in the browser’s side panel. It can read the page you’re on and act on it, so you can ask it to summarise a long contract, draft a follow-up from the CRM record in front of you, or build a table in a spreadsheet. In agent mode, it searches, clicks, and types its way through a multi-step task while you watch.


The models that drive this agent are chosen by your admins: we support Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Gemini natively, or, for customers who also have Netskope Skylight AI Gateway, you can add a custom or self-hosted model, for example one running on Amazon Bedrock. Each model connects with the company’s own API key, so people use the AI the company licenses and manages (with all of its superior security controls) instead of a personal or shadow account.


## Policy control for every browser prompt and agent action


The native Enterprise Browser agent is governed by the same browser controls as the person using it. If policy stops someone typing, pasting, or taking screenshots in an app, the agent will hit the same wall. And every site the agent visits still passes through Netskope One Next Gen SWG, with real-time data loss prevention (DLP) and threat protection.


Of course, you also connect **Netskope Skylight AI Guardrails** , automatically filtering prompts and responses for harmful or policy-violating content, identifying and blocking the output of patented, copyrighted, or sensitive corporate data, and providing protection against jailbreaks, and prompt injection threats. In our own testing, an analyst asked the agent to research a list of contacts and build a shared sheet, which it did. When they then asked to find each person’s personal email and mobile number, AI Guardrails stopped the request, identifying the sensitive data, with a coaching message to explain to the user why the activity was blocked. Self-hosted models connect to the Enterprise Browser through **Netskope Skylight AI Gateway** , which authenticates each call, applies rate limits, and logs every request.


Agent task in the side panel with an AI Guardrails coaching message


## New: Protection that stops risk at the source


The final set of Enterprise Browser additions puts small AI models inside the browser itself. **Screen Share Guard** checks what’s on screen when someone starts sharing and warns them if it spots sensitive data, so they can fix it without the meeting grinding to a halt. Native phishing detection uses a second on-device model to flag pages that look like phishing before the user types a password.


The **AI Extension Risk Analyzer** gives every Chrome Web Store extension a risk score, a risk level, and a Netskope recommendation. When someone tries to install a free AI writing helper that wants access to every site, the browser checks it against your company’s risk tolerance and blocks it if it scores too high.


## One browser, one platform


Netskope One Enterprise Browser shares one policy engine, one console, and the NewEdge network with the rest of the Netskope One platform, so an AI rule you write once can follow users and agents from the browser side panel right into web AI apps or AI features of your corporate SaaS apps. For existing customers, these new agentic capabilities are automatically available, which means there’s nothing new to deploy and no additional cost.


[As recommended by Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/7211030) , most security teams have thus far just said no to AI browsers in the enterprise. Netskope One Enterprise Browser’s secure native AI gives them a reason to say yes: people get the AI they want, with agents to support their productivity, and the whole thing aligns with a unified governance for AI. If that’s a conversation you’d like to have, start it with your account team.
